title: ISic001274. Dedication to Demeter

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text of Gualtherus;
  • line.2: Δημήτηρ ἡ ἱερ[ὰ Tortorici; Δημήτρ[ι] ἱερ[όν Franz ap. CIG III 5649e

translation

Marta Fogagnolo

… Demeter the sacred …

commentary

Only seen by Gualtherus, and while Franz’ amendment is attractive (l. 2 Δημήτρ[ι] ἱερ[όν), it is difficult to see how exactly that is recovered from Gualtherus’ transcription. Gualtherus (1624, nr. 31) recognized in the traces at l. 1 a possible reference to the city or the inhabitants of Catania (Κ[αταναίων), even if the evidence is scanty for a similar suggestion. Tortorici suggests that the inscription may not be genuine, a result of antiquarian enthusiasm to attribute the ruins as the temple, although this would be a relatively early date for such invention. The cult of Demeter at Catania in the Hellenistic period is attested by a sanctuary and by a dedication to Demeter and Kore dating to the 2nd–1st century BC, I. Catania 1 (ISic003109)(l. Δάματρι καὶ [Κ]όραι), for which see Korhonen 2004, 146–147.
